topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by introducing the scope of the lecture and its learning objectives regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe traditional cancer interventions—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with the systemic toxicities and efflux pump mechanisms that limit their effectiveness.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address therapeutic strategies designed to selectively exploit specific cancer cell weaknesses, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair.

topics.label: Oncogenic kinase targeting, inhibitor mechanisms, and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the rationale of treating oncogene-addicted cancers with small-molecule kinase inhibitors, detailing their structural binding mechanisms, resistance mutations, bypass pathways, and metronomic dosing strategies.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss antibody-mediated therapeutics that selectively engage cell-surface receptors to trigger cytotoxicity or deliver attached chemotherapeutic payloads directly to cancer cells.

topics.label: Tumor immunology and immunotherapy strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical evidence for immune surveillance and the modern therapeutic approaches that reactivate or engineer T cells to target cancer antigens.

topics.label: Broader challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate historical trends in cancer mortality alongside the clinical, biological, and ethical challenges involved in evaluating and implementing new cancer therapies.
